entries: {@i Choose A or B:} (A) 2 {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} ({@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}), {@item Robe|XPHB}, Spellbook, {@item Scholar's Pack|XPHB}, and 5 GP; or (B) 55 GP

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See {@book chapter 7|XPHB|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the {@filter Wizard spell list|spells|class=Wizard} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. {@spell Light|XPHB}, {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}, and {@spell Ray of Frost|XPHB} are recommended. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

entries.name: Spellbook
entries: Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting {@spell Identify|XPHB}. You determine the book's appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.

The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB}, {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB}, {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, {@spell Sleep|XPHB}, and {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB} are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} or your spellbook as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Wizard spells.

entries.name: Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook
entries: The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.

entries.name: Copying a Spell into the Book
entries: When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it's of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.

entries.name: Copying the Book
entries: You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

classFeature.name: Ritual Adept
entries: You can cast any spell as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} if that spell has the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

classFeature.name: Arcane Recovery
entries: You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Scholar
entries: While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, or {@skill Religion|XPHB}. You have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the chosen skill.

classFeature.name: Wizard Subclass
entries: You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Wizard level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Memorize Spell
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Wizard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Wizard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Wizard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Spell Mastery
entries: You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can study your spellbook and replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Spell Recall|XPHB} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Signature Spells
entries: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Abjurer
entries: {@i Shield Companions and Banish Foes}

Your study of magic is focused on spells that block, banish, or protect—ending harmful effects, banishing evil influences, and protecting the weak. Abjurers are sought when baleful spirits require exorcism, when locations must be guarded against magical spying, and when portals to other planes of existence must be closed. Adventuring parties value Abjurers for the protection they provide against a variety of hostile magic and other attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Abjuration Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Abjuration school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=A}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Abjuration school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Ward
entries: You can weave magic around yourself for protection. When you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, you can simultaneously use a strand of the spell's magic to create a magical ward on yourself that lasts until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The ward has a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum equal to twice your Wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward takes the damage instead, and if you have any Resistances or Vulnerabilities, apply them before reducing the ward's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If the damage reduces the ward to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you take any remaining damage. While the ward has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it can't absorb damage, but its magic remains.

Whenever you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, the ward regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice the level of the spell slot. Alternatively, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a spell slot, and the ward regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice the level of the spell slot expended.
Once you create the ward, you can't create it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Projected Ward
entries: When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause your Arcane Ward to absorb that damage. If this damage reduces the ward to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the warded creature takes any remaining damage. If that creature has any Resistances or Vulnerabilities, apply them before reducing the ward's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Breaker
entries: You always have the {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} and {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} spells prepared. In addition, you can cast {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to its ability check.
When you cast either spell with a spell slot, that slot isn't expended if the spell fails to stop a spell.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells, and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage of spells.

subclassFeature.name: Diviner
entries: {@i Learn the Secrets of the Multiverse}

The counsel of a Diviner is sought by those who want a clearer understanding of the past, present, and future. As a Diviner, you strive to part the veils of space, time, and consciousness. You work to master spells of discernment, remote viewing, supernatural knowledge, and foresight.

subclassFeature.name: Divination Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Divination school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=D}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Divination school|spells|class=Wizard|school=D} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Portent
entries: Glimpses of the future begin to press on your awareness. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can replace any {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} made by you or a creature that you can see with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll, and you can replace a roll in this way only once per turn.
Each foretelling roll can be used only once. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you lose any unused foretelling rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Expert Divination
entries: Casting Divination spells comes so easily to you that it expends only a fraction of your spellcasting efforts. When you cast a Divination spell using a level 2+ spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the slot you expended and can't be higher than level 5.

subclassFeature.name: The Third Eye
entries: You can increase your powers of perception. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose one of the following benefits, which lasts until you start a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

entries.name: Greater Comprehension
entries: You can read any language.

entries.name: See Invisibility
entries: You can cast {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Greater Portent
entries: The visions in your dreams intensify and paint a more accurate picture in your mind of what is to come. Roll three d20s for your Portent feature rather than two.

subclassFeature.name: Evoker
entries: {@i Create Explosive Elemental Effects}

Your studies focus on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some Evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast armies from afar. Others use their power to protect others, while some seek their own gain.

subclassFeature.name: Evocation Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Evocation school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=V}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Cantrip
entries: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Sculpt Spells
entries: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

subclassFeature.name: Empowered Evocation
entries: Whenever you cast a Wizard spell from the Evocation school, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

subclassFeature.name: Overchannel
entries: You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you take {@damage 2d12} Necrotic damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}.
Each time you use this feature again before finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the Necrotic damage per spell level increases by {@damage 1d12}.

subclassFeature.name: Illusionist
entries: {@i Weave Subtle Spells of Deception}
You specialize in magic that dazzles the senses and tricks the mind, and the illusions you craft make the impossible seem real.

subclassFeature.name: Illusion Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Illusion school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=I}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Illusion school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Illusions
entries: You can cast Illusion spells without providing Verbal components, and if an Illusion spell you cast has a range of 10+ feet, the range increases by 60 feet.

You also know the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Wizard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. You can create both a sound and an image with a single casting of {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB}, and you can cast it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Phantasmal Creatures
entries: You always have the {@spell Summon Beast|XPHB} and {@spell Summon Fey|XPHB} spells prepared. Whenever you cast either spell, you can change its school to Illusion, which causes the summoned creature to appear spectral. You can cast the Illusion version of each spell without expending a spell slot, but casting it without a slot halves the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Once you cast either spell without a spell slot, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can cast the spell in that way again.

subclassFeature.name: Illusory Self
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to interpose an illusory duplicate of yourself between the attacker and yourself. The attack automatically misses you, then the illusion dissipates.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Illusory Reality
entries: You have learned to weave shadow magic into your illusions to give them a semi-reality. When you cast an Illusion spell with a spell slot, you can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. You can do this on your turn as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while the spell is ongoing. The object remains real for 1 minute, during which it can't deal damage or give any conditions. For example, you can create an illusion of a bridge over a chasm and then make it real and cross it.

subclassFeature.name: Bladesinger
entries: {@i Wield Weapon and Wizardry in Elegant Tandem}

Bladesingers master a tradition of wizardry that incorporates swordplay and dance. In combat, a Bladesinger uses intricate, elegant maneuvers that fend off harm and allow the Bladesinger to channel magic into devastating attacks and a cunning defense. Many who have observed a Bladesinger at work remember the display as one of the more beautiful experiences in their life—a glorious dance accompanied by a singing blade.

Bladesinging is associated with the ancient elven societies that first mastered the art and coined the term. Even today, most Bladesingers still hail from old elven realms, such as Myth Drannor, or from non-elven societies that share land and history with elves, such as the Silver Marches. Wherever they hail from, Bladesingers take their talents all across the Realms to help common people and perform heroic deeds. Most communities greet the arrival of a Bladesinger as a good omen.

subclassFeature.name: Bladesong
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you invoke an elven magic called the Bladesong, provided you aren't wearing armor or using a Shield.

The Bladesong lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, if you don armor or a Shield, or if you use two hands to make an attack with a weapon. You can dismiss the Bladesong at any time (no action required).

While the Bladesong is active, you gain the following benefits. You can invoke the Bladesong a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You regain one expended use when you use Arcane Recovery.

entries.name: Agility
entries: You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1), and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Bladework
entries: Whenever you attack with a weapon with which you have proficiency, you can use your Intelligence modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity.

entries.name: Focus
entries: When you make a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the total.

subclassFeature.name: Training in War and Song
entries: You gain proficiency with all Melee Martial weapons that don't have the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} or {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} property. You can use a Melee weapon with which you have proficiency as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Wizard spells.
You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}, {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast {@filter one of your Wizard cantrips that has a casting time of an action|spells|level=0|class=wizard|cast time=action} in place of one of those attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Song of Defense
entries: When you take damage while your Bladesong is active, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend one spell slot and reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to five times the spell slot's level.

subclassFeature.name: Song of Victory
entries: After you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can make one attack with a weapon as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Conjurer
entries: {@i Step Across Space and Call Creatures from Thin Air}

A Conjurer considers distance and matter to be flexible guidelines rather than physical laws. Conjurers master magic that moves creatures instantly through space and summons creatures to fight on their behalf.

subclassFeature.name: Benign Transposition
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that you can see. Alternatively, you can choose a space within range that is occupied by a Medium or smaller creature. If that creature is willing, you both teleport, swapping places.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Conjuration Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Conjuration school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=C}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Conjuration school|spells|class=Wizard|school=C} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Distant Transposition
entries: The range of your Benign Transposition feature increases to 60 feet. Additionally, you can restore one use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Durable Summons
entries: When you cast a {@filter Conjuration spell|spells|school=C} to summon or create a creature using a spell slot, that creature gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Wizard level when it first appears. While it has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to every damage type except Force, Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Conjuration
entries: Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} on {@filter Conjuration spells|spells|school=C}.

subclassFeature.name: Splintered Summons
entries: When you use a spell slot to cast a {@filter Conjuration spell|spells|school=C} that summons a spirit whose stat block is included in the spell description, such as {@spell Summon Aberration|XPHB}, you can modify the spell to summon two creatures with the spell instead of one. Each creature is of the same kind, uses the stat block and rules denoted by the spell, and manifests in a different unoccupied space of your choice within the spell's range, but the summoned creatures' {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximums and current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are halved. If you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell, both creatures disappear.

Once you use this feature to modify a spell in this way, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Enchanter
entries: {@i Entrance and Beguile Others}
An Enchanter's magic clouds or captivates minds. Some Enchanters use their abilities to encourage peace and soften cruelty, while others use their mind-altering magic for selfish ends.

subclassFeature.name: Enchanting Conversationalist
entries: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}.
In addition, when you make an ability check with the chosen skill, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

subclassFeature.name: Enchantment Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Enchantment school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=E}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Enchantment school|spells|class=Wizard|school=E} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Hypnotic Presence
entries: Your charming words and enchanting gaze can enthrall another creature. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, choose one creature that you can see within 10 feet of yourself. If the target can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute or until the target is more than 10 feet away from you, the target can neither see nor hear you, or the target takes damage. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Split Enchantment
entries: When you use a spell slot to cast an {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E}, such as {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot to target an additional creature, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Instinctive Charm
entries: When a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attack misses instead, and if there is another creature within range of the attack other than the attacker, the attacker targets that creature with the triggering attack, using the same attack roll. If multiple creatures are within the attack's range, you choose which one to target.

Once you take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by casting an {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E} with a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Alter Memories
entries: You can make a creature unaware of your magical influence. When you cast an {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E} that imposes the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition using a spell slot, you can choose one creature targeted by the spell. That creature remains unaware of being {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you.

In addition, once before the spell ends, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to force the chosen creature to make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can make the creature lose a number of hours of its memories equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 hour lost). You can make the creature forget less time, and the amount of time can't exceed the duration of your {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E}.

subclassFeature.name: Necromancer
entries: {@i Command the Powers of Death and Undeath}

You explore the forces of life, death, and undeath. As a necromancer, you learn to manipulate the energy that animates all creatures, and you draw increasing power from the forbidden secrets in your spellbook. Though many see Necromancers as menacing or villainous, not all Necromancers are evil.

subclassFeature.name: Necromancy Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Necromancy school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=N}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Necromancy school|spells|class=Wizard|school=N} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Necromancy Spellbook
entries: Your spellbook's necromantic secrets grant you additional powers. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Necrotic Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Undead Familiar
entries: The {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell appears in your spellbook. When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: {@creature Skeleton|XMM} or {@creature Zombie|XMM} (see appendix B of the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB|11} for the familiar's stat block). When you choose one of the normal forms, you can choose Undead as its creature type.
Additionally, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

entries.name: Undead Vitality
entries: When you cast a {@filter Necromancy spell|spells|school=N} using a spell slot, you can choose an Undead creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the level of the spell slot expended plus your Wizard level.

subclassFeature.name: Grave Power
entries: You have discovered more necromantic insights and inscribed them in your spellbook. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Grave Resilience
entries: When you use Arcane Recovery, your {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, if any, decreases by 1.

entries.name: Overwhelming Necrosis
entries: Damage from your Wizard spells and Wizard features ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Undead Thralls
entries: You always have {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} prepared and can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can cast it in this way again. Whenever you start casting the spell, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.
In addition, while holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: Whenever you cast a {@filter Necromancy spell|spells|school=N} that creates or summons an Undead, the Undead's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum and current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} increase by a number equal to your Intelligence modifier plus half your Wizard level (round down).

entries.name: Withering Strike
entries: Whenever an Undead you control within 60 feet of you hits a creature with an attack roll, the Undead deals extra Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 Necrotic damage).

subclassFeature.name: Harvest Undead
entries: You have learned more secrets about the nuances of life and death. Immediately after you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} but aren't reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from taking damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce an Undead creature under your control that you can see to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You then immediately regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wizard level.

subclassFeature.name: Death's Master
entries: Abstruse rituals within your spellbook allow you mastery over undeath. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Bolster Undead
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose any number of Undead you have created or summoned with a {@filter Necromancy spell|spells|school=N} that are within 60 feet of you. Those Undead each gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wizard level. Once you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Extinguish Undead
entries: When an Undead creature you can see is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can cause it to explode with necrotic energy. Roll a number of d6s equal to half the creature's unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} (round up, minimum of {@damage 1d6}), and add them together. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the Undead makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled and can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only. When you use this feature to explode an Undead creature you don't control, you must take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend a level 5+ spell slot to do so.

subclassFeature.name: Transmuter
entries: {@i Transform Energy and Matter}
You study spells that modify energy and matter—to you, the world is eminently mutable. Using your magic, you become a smith at reality's forge.
Some Transmuters are tinkerers and pranksters. Others seek the power to make and destroy worlds.

subclassFeature.name: Transmutation Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Transmutation school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=T}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Transmutation school|spells|class=Wizard|school=T} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Transmuter's Stone
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create a magic stone that lasts until you use this feature again. The stone is a Tiny object, and you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Wizard spells. A creature with the stone in its possession gains proficiency in Constitution saving throws and one of the following benefits, which you choose when you create the stone. You can change the stone's benefit when you cast a {@filter Transmutation spell|spells|school=T} using a spell slot.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: The bearer gains {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet or increases the range of its {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} by 60 feet.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: The bearer gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage (your choice each time you choose this benefit).

entries.name: Speed
entries: The bearer's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Wondrous Alteration
entries: You always have the {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While under the effects of {@spell Alter Self|XPHB}, you gain an additional benefit for each of its options.

entries.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: While underwater, you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Change Appearance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: The damage of your new growth increases to {@damage 2d6} damage of the type associated with the growth. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Empowered Transmutation
entries: When you use a spell slot to cast a {@filter Transmutation spell|spells|school=T} that doesn't make an attack roll or force a saving throw, such as {@spell Fly|XPHB} or {@spell Magic Weapon|XPHB}, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Stone
entries: Your Transmuter's Stone is more versatile. When you create your Transmuter's Stone, you can choose up to two benefits. You can choose each option other than {@b Resistance} only once. If you choose {@b Resistance} twice, you must choose different damage types. You can change either or both benefits when you cast a {@filter Transmutation spell|spells|school=T} using a spell slot.
In addition, the following are now among your benefit options for Transmuter's Stone.

entries.name: Mighty Build
entries: The bearer has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength saving throws. The bearer also counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity.

entries.name: Tremorsense
entries: The bearer gains {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Shape-Shifter
entries: You always have the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

In addition, when you target yourself with the spell, you can modify the spell to gain the benefits below. Once you modify the spell using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Game Statistics
entries: In addition to retaining the features specified in the spell, you retain your memories and ability to communicate. You also retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; proficiencies; class features; and feats.

entries.name: Transmute Spells
entries: While shape-shifted, you can cast spells, but only {@filter Transmutation spells|spells|school=T} that don't have a Material component that has a specified cost or that is consumed by the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Master Transmuter
entries: While you carry your Transmuter's Stone, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to consume the reserve of transmutation magic stored inside and choose one of the following benefits. After you use the stone in this way, it crumbles to dust. You can prevent the stone from crumbling by expending a level 7+ spell slot as part of the {@action Magic|XPHB} action you take using this feature.

entries.name: Major Transformation
entries: You can transmute one nonmagical object—no larger than a 10-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} or eight connected 5-foot Cubes—into another nonmagical object of similar size and mass and of equal or lesser value. You must spend 10 minutes handling the object to transform it.

entries.name: Panacea
entries: You touch a creature as part of this {@action Magic|XPHB} action, and the target regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum (round down). The target is cured of all magical contagions, and any curses affecting the target are lifted, including the target's {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to a cursed item. If the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} or {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition, those conditions end.

entries.name: Restore Life
entries: You cast the {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot, using the stone in place of the required Material components.

entries.name: Restore Youth
entries: You touch one willing creature as part of this {@action Magic|XPHB} action, and the target's {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, if any, decreases to 0, and it permanently appears {@dice 3d10} years younger, to a minimum of young adulthood.
